evidence: nginx-bundle-cert-then-intermediate (ssl_base.pp:79-81): with letsencrypt_certificate=false and myservice 'nginx' (ssl_nginx.pp) the bundle is ${ssl_certs_dir}/${myprefix}.${myservice}.bundle.crt = /etc/ssl/certs/p8test.nginx.bundle.crt on Debian, first fragment from <prefix>.crt and second from <prefix>.intermediate.crt; the probe's 2 certificates with the first one's subject CN=p8test.invalid (the fixture's server cert) tests exactly that order

nginx-bundle-cert-then-intermediate (ssl_base.pp:100-107): concat with mode '0644' and owner $owner (default 'root'); the probe's 'root 644' matches the defaults ssl_nginx passes through (no owner/group given)

bundle-certificate-matches-the-key (ssl_base.pp:77-81): key from <prefix>.key and first certificate from <prefix>.crt of the same prefix; comparing the public keys of the bundle's first certificate and /etc/ssl/private/p8test.key tests that the class installs a usable pair; the mismatch swaps only the key (the node's Puppet agent key, a different key), which must change the verdict, and it failed after apply as required

purpose covered: Purpose matches ssl_nginx.pp (ssl_base with myservice/myservicename nginx, letsencrypt default false) and ssl_base's header (key file, service bundle, restart on change). Tested: key at /etc/ssl/private/p8test.key root:root 0600; bundle root 0644 with server cert then intermediate; cert matches key (with mismatch control); a hand-changed bundle and, separately, a hand-changed key are put back by the node's agent run and nginx restarts (new MainPID, active) - the reviewer run's agent logs show only the corrective content change and Service[nginx] 'Triggered refresh from 1 event' each time, so the restart is caused by the class's notify. Mutating checks declare all they change (the drift line, PID/digest notes under /run/p8test-sslnginx) and are judged on read-only effects, not the action's output. Left out: RedHat paths (ssl_base.pp:56-68) - uncovered row honest: phase3.py selects one node per class via nodes.select(cls) and the set holds one fixed Debian path set, so a rhel9 run of this class needs a per-node set capability (same lifted_by as other approved sets); the Let's Encrypt branch is correctly excluded as unreachable (ssl_nginx passes no letsencrypt_certificate). nginx actually serving TLS with the bundle needs a vhost declared by other classes (ssl_nginx declares none), so it is not this class's outcome.
